newsitem.title: USA: Supervalu to divest stake in ShopKo.
newsitem.headline: Supervalu to divest stake in ShopKo.

text.p: Food company Supervalu Inc. said Friday it would divest its 46 percent stake in regional discount retailer ShopKo Stores Inc. in a two-part transaction that calls for a $150 million stock buyback and a secondary public offering.
The move will end a 26-year relationship between the two companies. Supervalu bought ShopKo in 1971 and then sold 54 percent of its stock in a 1991 public offering.

Green Bay, Wis.-based ShopKo said it may have to take a one-time pre-tax charge $8.5 million to cover costs associated with the transaction. It also said that it will postpone its June 18 annual shareholder meeting until after the deal is completed.

Under the plan, ShopKo will buy back 8.2 million shares of its common stock held by Supervalu for $18.35 per share. The buyback price represents a discount of 65 cents per share from the closing price of ShopKo common stock on April 24, 1997.
The second part of the transaction calls for a secondary public offering of 6.6 million shares of ShopKo common stock, representing the balance of Supervalu's investment.
The two transactions are contingent upon each other.
Minneapolis-based Supervalu previously had announced its intention to divest its investment in ShopKo.
The two companies had been expected to move quickly to provide an exit strategy for Supervalu following the collapse earlier this month of ShopKo's proposed $1 billion merger with Phar-Mor Inc.

"These transactions provide an exit strategy for Supervalu which benefits our remaining shareholders, removes the overhang on the market for our securities and preserves our financial flexibility to grow through acquisitions and make future capital expenditures," said ShopKo Chief Executive Officer Dale Kramer.
Supervalu said it will consider several alternatives for the proceeds of the transaction, including debt reduction or acquisitions in its core wholesale or retail food operations.

Upon the closing of the transactions, Supervalu Chairman, President and Chief Executive Mike Wright, who also served as chairman of ShopKo, and Jeff Girard, Supervalu's executive vice president and chief financial officer, will step down from ShopKo's board of directors,
The companies said that Kramer is expected to be named chairman of Shopko and maintain his current position as president and chief executive.
In a conference call with analysts, ShopKo said it is working with Salomon Brothers to consider growth alternatives, possibly through acquisitions.
However, Kramer noted, "At this time, there are no discussions taking place with any major retailer."
He said ShopKo thinks it can expand by 15 stores per year over the next three years in areas contiguous to existing markets.
ShopKo shares rose 12.5 cents to $19.125 on the New York Stock Exchange. The stock of Supervalu gained 37.5 cents to $29.625, also on NYSE.

ShopKo operates 130 stores in 15 states, mostly in the Upper Midwest, Mountain and Pacific Northwest states. It also has a wholly-owned subsidiary, ProVantage Inc., which specialises in prescription benefit management, benefit management and health decision support services.
Supervalu, a food distributor and retailer, serves more than 4,300 stores in 48 states, and 611 limited assortment stores through its Save-A-Lot operations.
